mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue original certificate, notarize if required, obtain apostille from the competent authority of the issuing country, then obtain a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille states: issue original certificate, notarize, authenticate through the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize at the Consular Section of the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that country, then obtain a certified Korean translation. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: produce original certificate, notarize if required, apostille by the competent Hague authority, then certified Korean translation. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, UBO, signatory, and material counterparty must be screened at formation and continuously thereafter against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and all OFAC embargo programs, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation consolidated list, and the Republic of Korea FIU watch lists and domestic asset-blocking designations. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their relatives, and close associates; it requires senior management approval, documented source of wealth and funds, and ongoing transaction monitoring. All screening results and risk scoring must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea and the National Tax Service Hometax business registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Commercial Act requires the corporate name of a Korean limited liability company to be expressed in the Korean alphabet and to end with the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. The four-tier naming convention requires: first, a distinctive trade element; second, a business-purpose descriptor; third, a legal-form indicator; and fourth, the Yuhan Hoesa suffix. The Hangul legal name controls for registration, VAT, tax invoices, and bank accounts; a foreign-language e-commerce brand may be filed as an additional trade name after the Hangul name is accepted, and must be transliterated phonetically if used in the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry office rejects the proposed company name, the applicant must first correct the defect and resubmit through the Internet Registry Office. If the rejection is contested, an appeal may be filed with the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, amended Articles of Association, a fresh name-clearance search, and a written statement of grounds. The court may reverse the registry decision or order the registration; alternatively, the applicant may delete the prohibited or sensitive token and refile.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for this industry. The Commercial Act and National Tax Service require a genuine business place for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painted limited edition statues. A virtual office may supplement, but cannot replace, a physical studio, workshop, warehouse, or home office where production, storage, and management actually occur. Korean municipal tax authorities and banks will reject a registered address that is only a mailbox, particularly for VAT business registration, corporate bank account opening, and settlement through Stripe or PayPal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 20-35% for a low-risk e-commerce and statue business operating from a registered physical studio; 40-60% if the company uses only a virtual mailbox, submits irregular tax invoices, or reports zero sales while maintaining a bank account. Checklist for on-site inspection: lease or ownership documentation, utility bills in the company name, casting and painting equipment, inventory and finished goods, preorder and settlement records from Stripe and PayPal, purchase invoices, payroll or outsourcing contracts, corporate seal, statutory books, and visible company signage. The municipal tax office and district registry can conduct unannounced visits to verify substantive business presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last consolidated and amended; today in force under Book III, Chapter V 'Limited Company,' Articles 543 through 619), including Articles 543 (definition and limited liability), 544 (formation and content of articles of incorporation), 548 (time of incorporation/registration), 555 (directors and representation), 565 (duties of directors), 586 (written resolutions), and 604 (auditor provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, e-filed through the Supreme Court of Korea I-REGI Internet Registry System at www.iros.go.kr; post-registration corporate extracts are issued by the Court Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Korean Commercial Act, accompanied by the executed Articles of Incorporation, capital contribution proof, lease/registered-office consent, officer consents, and powers of attorney.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. The full amount of each member's cash contribution must be deposited in a provisional bank account opened in the name of the proposed company before registration, and a bank balance certificate must be filed with the registry. Non-cash contributions require independent valuation and actual transfer of title. No blocked escrow or regulator-managed escrow account is required; the deposited capital may be transferred to the corporate operating account after registration, but it must remain accurately stated as paid-in capital.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the electronic portal 'Home Tax Service (HTS)' at www.hometax.go.kr and the customs trade portal 'UNI-PASS' administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The statutory tax identification number in South Korea is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which also serves as the Value-Added Tax registration number. A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must first obtain corporate existence under the Korean Commercial Act and then apply for BRN registration with the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office or place of business. The application must be filed through Home Tax Service or in person at the NTS district tax office using the standard Application for Business Registration, along with the entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign certificate of good standing or equivalent foreign registration evidence, proof of domestic business address, identification of the representative, and, for a foreign non-resident entrepreneur without a domestic place of business, a duly executed power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes. NTS reviews the submitted dossier and issues the BRN; after registration, the entity is entered into the NTS taxpayer master file, enabled for electronic tax invoice issuance through Home Tax Service, and subject to periodic VAT filing obligations. There is no minimum capital requirement, and non-resident ownership is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Corporation Tax Act and is taxed on its worldwide income at the entity level; it is not a pass-through entity, and its shareholders are separately taxed on dividends except where treaty withholding or special tax rates apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election. The Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation for Korean corporate income tax and VAT purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Korea applies the OECD BEPS hybrid mismatch rules through statutory override rather than elective or check-the-box mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold applies to the corporate entity. Any person carrying on a business in South Korea, including a Yuhan Hoesa, must obtain a Business Registration Number and register for VAT before or immediately upon commencement of business regardless of projected turnover. For a foreign non-resident supplier without a domestic place of business supplying taxable goods or services in Korea, registration is likewise triggered by the commencement of Korean taxable business activity; the individual simplified taxable person regime is not available to corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea does not impose a pre-invoice real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping mandate comparable to Italian or LATAM clearance models. Instead, all registered corporate taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) through the NTS Home Tax Service electronic tax invoice infrastructure, either via the HTS web portal, NTS-certified ERP connectors, or NTS XML/JSON web service APIs. The e-tax invoice must contain the fully registered BRNs of supplier and recipient, the taxable supply value, VAT amount, and statutory data fields, and must be transmitted to NTS for cross-matching. NTS operates a continuous purchase-and-sales invoice matching and audit mining system; any mismatch or late transmission triggers penalties and tax audit attention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, including polyresin statues and garage kits, qualify for a 0% VAT rate under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods physically leave South Korea pursuant to an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, the exporter retains verifiable customs clearance and transportation evidence, and the export proceeds are eventually received through a foreign exchange settlement channel authorized by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Qualifying services supplied outside Korea and digital services consumed by non-resident users may also qualify for zero-rating, but for resin statue garage kits the standard export-of-goods pathway under KCS Tariff and VAT rules applies. The zero-rating claim is substantiated by the exporter's complete export transaction file, not merely by the invoice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Acceptance Certificate issued by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading for ocean freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing physical export from Korea
Sales contract or confirmed purchase order from the foreign buyer
Foreign Exchange Remittance and Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Customs export clearance manifest or KCS official export record where requested by the National Tax Service
Certificate of Origin (only where a preferential tariff claim is made under a free trade agreement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to joint audit scrutiny by the National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service. If the exporter cannot produce the required KCS export declaration, shipping documents, and bank settlement evidence, NTS will treat the supply as a taxable domestic transaction, reassess VAT at the standard 10% rate, deny the corresponding input VAT credit and any VAT refund previously paid, impose additional tax penalties for incorrect returns, and assess statutory interest. Deliberate creation of false export declarations, forged shipping documents, or sham foreign exchange settlements to obtain zero-rating constitutes tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may expose the entity, its responsible representative, and the appointed tax representative to criminal fines and imprisonment, in addition to venue-wide export privilege restrictions and clawback of all improperly claimed zero-rated VAT benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the primary FX policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Bank of Korea Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely open current account but maintains a reporting-based foreign exchange system rather than a free-floating unrestricted regime. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), both capital and current account transactions are generally liberalized, but any transfer exceeding USD 5,000 (or equivalent) must be reported to the supervising foreign exchange bank, and transactions above USD 100,000 require a certificate of receipt or payment and periodic reporting to the Korea Customs Service or the Bank of Korea. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, profit repatriation, and intercompany loans, are subject to a prior declaration or notification regime, and permission may be required if the transaction is deemed to pose risks to market stability or violates public interest. For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) engaged in high-end resin statue production, the practical convertibility is strong for trade and service receipts, but profit remittance to non-resident shareholders triggers a 22% withholding tax on dividends (unless tax treaty relief applies), and banks will require proof of tax clearance and a certified foreign exchange remittance report. Inbound foreign currency for pre-orders and export collections must be either converted into Korean won or held in a foreign currency account with a domestic licensed bank; there is no mandatory surrender obligation for all proceeds, but the exporter must report the receipts within 30 days of receipt via the trade system. Dividend remittances require the target entity to submit board resolutions, audited financial statements, tax payment receipts, and a certified statement that the distribution meets the capital impairment test under the Korean Commercial Act. Overall, the regime is compliant for legitimate commercial flows but demands rigorous documentary trails for every cross-border movement, especially when the beneficial owner is a non-resident individual or holding structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korean law does not impose a blanket surrender requirement. Export proceeds in foreign currency may be retained in a foreign currency account at a domestic licensed bank, but the receiving entity must file an inward remittance report with the bank within 30 days of receipt. For all export contracts exceeding USD 10,000, the Korean exporter must obtain a contract number from the Korea Customs Service and settle the proceeds within the prescribed period (typically 180 days from shipment date, extendable upon application). If the proceeds are received via a non-regular bank account or through a third-party payment intermediary (e.g., Stripe, PayPal), the entity must additionally submit a 'Reference to Inward Remittance' form and the underlying invoice to the bank to prove the commercial nature of the inflow and to avoid being classified as an unlicensed money transfer. No mandatory conversion into KRW is required, but any conversion must be executed at a market rate through a licensed foreign exchange bank. For pre-order deposits received as advance payments, the advance portion must be registered as an export advance and is subject to a 90-day settlement requirement unless an extension is granted by the bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for direct EMI banking. South Korea does not permit foreign or domestic fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) to hold fiat deposits or provide corporate IBAN-style foreign currency accounts that can be used for settlement. The Electronic Financial Transactions Act (EFTA) restricts deposit-taking activities to licensed banks, and non-bank EMIs may only operate as payment facilitators (e.g., issuing prepaid wallets) with mandatory backing by a domestic bank's trust account. For a Yuhan Hoesa receiving pre-orders via Stripe or PayPal, these PSPs are treated as payment settlement proxies; the actual settlement must be directed into a KRW or USD corporate account held at a licensed Korean bank. Any fintech such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex cannot be used to receive or hold export proceeds in Korea because they are not licensed as banks under the Banking Act and their aggregated accounts violate the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act's requirement that all cross-border receipts be credited to a named customer account at a domestic bank. Moreover, Korea's Real Name Financial Transaction Act mandates that all transactions be traceable to a legal entity's verified registration number (business registration number) and that foreign currency payments be matched with the underlying customs declaration. Therefore, the viable path is to maintain a fresh-currency account with a Tier-1 bank and use Stripe/PayPal only as a technology gateway that settles through the bank's acquiring relationship, not as an independent settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with foreign directors (non-resident ownership allowed), Korean banks require physical presence of at least one statutory director (or the authorized corporate officer) at the first onboarding interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for foreign-owned entities unless the bank has a special 'non-face-to-face' opening procedure for small-amount domestic entities; those procedures require a locally issued mobile identity (Korean resident registration or alien registration) which a foreign director typically lacks. Therefore, the mandated workflow is: (1) file the incorporation with the Korean Commercial Registry; (2) obtain a corporate seal certificate and business registration certificate; (3) the foreign director must travel to Korea (unless he/she already has a Korean visa and a registered seal) to physically appear at a designated branch of the Tier-1 bank; (4) if the director cannot travel, a power of attorney (POA) authenticated by a Korean consulate in the director's home country, accompanied by the director's passport copy and a verification call/video interview, may be accepted on a discretionary basis by some banks, but 90% of branches will still require a local representative to attend with the original corporate seal. The safest route is to appoint a Korean resident compliance officer or legal representative with a valid INSIGHT certificate and a company seal, and to have the foreign director execute a POA in front of a Korean notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder with layered ownership and unverified beneficial owner (UBO) due to a foreign holding in a tax-secrecy jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full organizational chart of every shareholder up to the ultimate individual, certified by the foreign corporate registry; audited financial statements or a notarized certificate of good standing for each intermediate entity; passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners with 6-month validity; and a sworn affidavit that no politically exposed person (PEP) is involved. The dossier must be accompanied by a professional legal opinion from a Korean DRA (Designated Representative Attorney) confirming the substitution of absence of beneficial ownership information is impossible under the FIU guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-order stream from Stripe and PayPal creates aggregated incoming payments from thousands of consumer accounts, making it impossible to match each payment to an underlying export invoice and potentially triggering unlicensed money transmission red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement a dedicated payment reconciliation sub-ledger that maps each Stripe/PayPal payout to the corresponding sales order, customer name (masked), invoice number, and customs HS code (HS-3926 for resin products). For each settlement cycle, supply the bank with a consolidated payout report generated by the payment gateway, a contract with the gateway provider showing the merchant-ID and settlement terms, and an internal audit trail showing that no payable to a third party is made without an invoice. Additionally, file a standing 'Advance Export Declaration' with the Korea Customs Service for the online sales model, and submit the customs declaration number to the bank before the funds are credited.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value individual consumer payments for limited-edition statues may exceed typical trafficking thresholds and trigger unexplained wealth reports, especially when refunds and chargebacks are made across Thailand and EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a full Know-Your-Collector (KYC) file for every consumer order above USD 5,000, including identity verification, shipping address validation, and a recorded history of prior purchases. For bank onboarding, present a written compliance manual and a chargeback/refund policy that complies with Korean E-commerce Act; show the bank a monthly status report of open pre-order backlogs, production progress photos, and inventory tracking to prove the funds are used for manufacturing, not for underground transfers. Also provide the bank with a legal opinion that the entity's NFTs or digital content licensing (if any) is separate from the resin statue revenue stream.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The business name 'Yuhan Hoesa' and the product category 'garage kits' might be mistaken for counterfeit or unlicensed toy manufacturing, leading to IP infringement screening flags at the bank's sanctions/denied-party filter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide registered trademark certificates for all brand names and designs, a license agreement with the IP owner (if the resin statue is inspired by 3rd-party content), and evidence of original design registration from the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO). Also submit the ISIC 3240 classification certificate and, if applicable, the Korean product safety certification (KC mark) not required for non-character adult collectibles, but include a pro-forma certificate of origin to prove lawful manufacture. If the brand uses any celebrity or anime likeness, supply the official licensing contract or a waiver letter from the copyright holder; otherwise, provide an independent legal opinion that the product is pure original art, not a counterfeit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Korean LLC receiving shareholder loans or equity injection from abroad, the investor must submit an 'Assignment of Foreign Exchange', and the funds must be credited to a dedicated domestic bank account under the entity's name. If the investment exceeds USD 100,000, the entity must lodge the foreign direct investment (FDI) report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Korea Trade Insurance Corp (designated agent) within 30 day of the payment. The wire should be initiated via SWIFT MT103 with the remittance reason code (e.g., 'A522 – FDI equity contribution' or 'A523 – intercompany loan'). The receiving bank must verify the gross amount against the report and may require the entity to present the corporate seal and the original investment report before releasing funds for operational use. If the inbound is advance payment for pre-orders from overseas consumers, the routing should be: consumer payment → Stripe/PayPal payout in usd → settlement to the bank's acquiring account → automatic or manual sweep to the company's USD current account → then either retain in USD or convert to KRW via a spot transaction with a licensed bank. Every conversion above USD 20,000 must be supported by an invoice and a customs export declaration number to avoid the aggregation concern. For capital verification, the entity must produce an audited confirmation from a Korean certified public accountant that the book capital matches the reports filed with the BOK.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for production materials, molds, and overseas subcontracting should be executed via SWIFT MT103 with corresponding purpose codes ('D830 – payment for imports' or 'D840 – royalty payments'). For high-value trade contracts exceeding USD 50,000, a Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) or an irrevocable Letter of Credit (L/C) is recommended to mitigate counterparty fraud; the L/C must be issued through a domestic bank and comply with UCP600 rules. Payments to suppliers in China or Japan for raw resin and pigments must be supported by the purchase order, customs import declaration, and a bill of lading or air waybill. The bank will require the entity to maintain a 'foreign currency account' with a positive balance to make direct debits, or to convert KRW to the target currency at spot through the treasury desk. For recurring subscriptions to 3D-printing software and design tools, the entity may set up a recurring instruction for amounts below USD 5,000 using the same MT103 channel, but each transaction must be aggregated and reported monthly to the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (dollar/KRW or dollar/JPY) for up to 12 months, only to hedge committed commercial exposures and requiring underlying export/import contracts or pre-order backlog evidence

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts with maturities up to 6 months, allowed for trade receivables when the entity cannot physically deliver KRW, but must be documented with a future export invoice
Currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS) are permitted for intra-group loans exceeding USD 1 million, solely to cover principal and interest mismatch; speculative positions are strictly prohibited

Cross-currency option collars (zero-cost collars) may be arranged through the bank's treasury desk for hedging the KRW depreciation risk on USD-denominated pre-orders, but require a half-yearly risk management policy and board approval

All hedging instruments must be booked with a licensed Korean bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; any netting of profit/loss in FX derivatives must be reported to the National Tax Service for transfer pricing if the counterparty is a related party

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December: no later than 31 March of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year: no later than the last day of the third month following the fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or insufficient returns attract an additional tax of 20% of the underpaid corporate tax, or 40% if the understatement is intentional or grossly negligent; late-paid corporate tax accrues statutory delay interest at 0.022% per day from the day after the due date until paid; prolonged nonpayment authorizes NTS asset seizure, business registration cancellation, and may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off of the dormant entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through local tax e-filing channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year: no later than 30 April of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year: within four months after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underreporting incurs a 20% additional tax; unpaid local corporate income tax is subject to local tax arrears charges at the statutory daily rate and eventual administrative collection or asset attachment; persistent nonfiling can trigger business registration cancellation and administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary and Semi-Annual Final Returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the HomeTax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary returns are due on 25 April, 25 July, 25 October, and 25 January for the respective calendar quarter windows; semi-annual final returns are due on 25 July for the first half-year and 25 January for the second half-year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT penalties under the VAT Act include 20% of unpaid VAT for unfaithful returns and 40% for false or deceptive returns; late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.022% per day; serial nonfiling may lead to estimated assessment by the NTS, seizure of assets, and cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and External Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of Korea via the DART system, with a copy included in or attached to the NTS corporate tax return when a statutory audit is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the statutory corporate tax filing deadline, 31 March for calendar-year companies, and in all cases before the ordinary members' meeting is held; an audited non-listed company must submit the external audit report to the FSS within two weeks after receipt from the auditor, and no later than 90 days after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or submit a required audit report is penalized under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others with administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 23,100) for the company and KRW 20,000,000 (approx. USD 15,400) for responsible directors; the FSS may order corrective measures and the NTS may disregard the unaudited financial statements, exposing the company to accuracy-based tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Members' General Meeting and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; no central filing is required for a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held not later than three months after the close of the fiscal year, which for a calendar-year entity is by 31 March of the following year, unless the articles of incorporation prescribe an earlier date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual members' meeting does not create a direct government filing fee, but the failure may constitute a breach of duty by the managing director, trigger member derivative claims, and, if annual financial statements are not approved within the fiscal year, impair the effective use of tax-loss carryforwards and expose the company to tax administration penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Membership Interest Transfer Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: For domestically sourced transfers: the Yuhan Hoesa's statutory Register of Members, with no central government filing; for foreign-invested transfers: the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any membership or equity interest transfer, pledge, acquisition, or other regulatory beneficial ownership change; annual confirmation is required at the ordinary members' meeting date and in the annual foreign-invested enterprise report where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the Register of Members will prevent the transferee from asserting the transfer against third parties; foreign-investor reporting failures are subject to administrative fines not exceeding KRW 10,000,000 (approx. USD 7,700), and may result in denial of foreign-investment tax benefits or remittance rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Profile Update for Representative, Director, and Principal Place of Business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service and concurrent local municipality business tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any change in the legal representative, director, registered address, trade name, principal business, or articles provisions relevant to the business registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed business registration amendment can generate a negligence penalty up to KRW 1,000,000 (approx. USD 770); a registered office without physical presence may invite an NTS field audit and, if no business office is found, administrative closure of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), applicable only if the Yuhan Hoesa qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the foreign-invested enterprise's fiscal year, which for a calendar-year entity is by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual foreign-invested enterprise management report may result in an administrative fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of favorable foreign-investment incentives, and delays or denial of foreign exchange remittance privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others, a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily subject to independent certified public accountant audit if it meets any of the following quantitative tests at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9,230,770 at KRW 1,300/USD); (ii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7,000,000,000 (approx. USD 5,384,620) and annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 5,000,000,000 (approx. USD 3,846,150); (iii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7,000,000,000 (approx. USD 5,384,620) and the company employed 50 or more full-time employees at the preceding fiscal year-end; (iv) the company is a subsidiary of an external-audit entity or is consolidated into an audited group; or (v) the company falls within special industry or public-interest categories designated by the Enforcement Decree, including financial services or public solicitation of investment. For a Yuhan Hoesa below these thresholds, a statutory audit is not legally mandated, although a bank, investor, licensor, or cross-border trading counterparty may contractually require one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For a Yuhan Hoesa subject to statutory audit, annual financial statements must be prepared under K-IFRS if the entity is a listed company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% top marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; 20% for income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 10% for the first KRW 200 million (plus 10% local surtax on the calculated corporate tax, aggregating to a maximum effective combined rate of 24.2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium enterprises (SMEs) may enjoy a reduced 10% rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. Additional incentives include R&D tax credits, investment tax credits for new-growth industries, foreign-investment tax holidays in free economic zones, and regional employment subsidies, subject to statutory requirements and the entity's actual substance. For a polyresin statue producer, the SME rate reduction and R&D credits for product mold development are the most likely benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement, together with required attached schedules, Form 1-1 through Form 1-8), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-Filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis); all corporations are also required to file an interim half-year provisional tax return and payment for the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year per Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act. For a calendar-year entity, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. Interim provisional returns are due within two months after the first half-year-end (e.g., July 31 for calendar-year taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Revenue (Sales of resin statues, limited editions, garage kits, preorder deposits recognized as revenue).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross worldwide sales after deducting sales discounts and returns. For sales to foreign distributors or related non-resident enterprises, use the actual transaction price but be prepared to adjust to the arm's length standard under Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act. Cross-border electronic payment fees from Stripe/PayPal must be properly recorded and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Goods Sold (polyresin raw materials, molds, direct labor, painting, packing, and manufacturing overhead).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When materials are imported from a foreign related supplier, ensure the purchase price is at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous comparables. Inflated inbound prices to strip profits from the Korean entity are a common audit target and may trigger transfer pricing adjustments and a 5% penalty on the overstated transaction amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Expenses (rent, salaries, utilities, shipping, marketing, platform fees, insurance, royalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties or management service fees paid to non-residents must be documented with contracts, have commercial substance, and be subject to the appropriate withholding tax. Deductions may be denied under Article 116 of the Corporate Tax Act if the actual recipient is unidentified or the expense lacks business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Income (gross profit less operating expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If operating income appears disproportionately low compared with industry profit data, the Korean tax authorities may re-examine intercompany pricing. The entity should maintain a realistic profit allocation derived from its functional profile, assets, and risks, particularly in its relationship with non-resident distributors or IP owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Operating Income and Expenses (foreign exchange gains/losses, interest income, dividends, donations, and other incidental items).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign parent companies or non-resident shareholders is subject to a rigorous thin capitalization test: interest attributable to debt exceeding a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio is disallowed per Article 53-1 of the Corporate Tax Act. Any foreign exchange losses from loans in foreign currencies must be supported by currency exposure and proper accounting.

Aggregate operating and non-operating items. Distributions or dividend declarations to non-resident shareholders are not deductible here; they are separately subject to dividend withholding tax when the shareholders receive them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss Carryforward Deduction (net operating losses from prior years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply eligible prior-year losses carried forward for up to ten years (five years for losses originating before 2019). A change of 50% or more in the ownership of a non-resident-controlled company may trigger the loss carryforward restriction under Article 45(3) of the Corporate Tax Act, so maintain full share-transfer records.

This is the final base multiplied by the statutory progressive rates. Because the entity is a Korean domestic corporation, its worldwide income is taxed. Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on this income until distribution; however, the entity must ensure that its share registry accurately reflects non-resident ownership for future withholding obligations.

Apply the progressive schedule to the taxable income: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% above KRW 20 billion. Add the 10% local surtax (local income tax surcharge) to the federal corporate tax. If foreign-source income is included, claim the foreign tax credit and attach the relevant schedule.

Deduct statutory tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credit, R&D credits, employment credits). Add any penalty surcharges for late or understated prior filings. For cross-border related-party transactions, failure to submit the foreign related-party transaction schedule (Form 2-2) results in a penalty of up to 5% of the transaction value under Article 11 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, Interim Provisional Tax, and Withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct the interim provisional tax already paid, any tax withheld on domestic investment income, and previous-year advance payments. Do not treat outbound dividend withholding tax as part of the corporate tax calculation; it is a separate shareholder obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final Tax Payable or Refund Due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any balance due by the statutory deadline. For a non-resident owned entity, ensure that the bank remittance of the final tax payment identifies the company tax ID. If the return claims a refund, the refund will be audited more strictly because of cross-border loss utilization and foreign tax credit claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers a penalty under Article 75 of the Corporate Tax Act: 20% of the unpaid tax if filed late without due cause, plus a daily surcharge of 0.03% on the unpaid amount. Underreporting penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes are 10% of the underreported tax (or 40% for fraudulent underreporting). Failure to disclose cross-border related-party transactions incurs a penalty of 5% of the transaction amount. Criminal penalties for intentional evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act range up to 10 years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding: 20% federal dividend withholding tax under Article 98(1) of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income surtax (10% surcharge on the federal WHT) under the Local Tax Act. A bilateral tax treaty may reduce this rate (commonly to 5% for substantial shareholdings and 15% for portfolio dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the country of residence; (2) file the 'Application for Non-Resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction' (Form 24-B) with the Korean paying company or directly with the competent Korean tax office through HomeTax prior to the dividend payment; (3) establish beneficial ownership of the dividend income and demonstrate that the shareholder is not a conduit; and (4) maintain the minimum shareholding during the record date and the period required by the DTA. The Korean payer must submit the approved application and documents together with the withholding return to secure the reduced rate. If the treaty rate is not applied at the time of payment, the excess withholding may be reclaimed via a refund application within the statutory period (generally three years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 20% federal WHT plus 2% local surcharge (22% total) under Article 98(1) of the Corporate Tax Act and the Local Tax Act. Treaty rates vary, frequently reducing interest and royalties to 0-15% depending on the treaty partner. For royalty payments, the Korean payer must also consider VAT and document the technical/industrial nature of the IP. For interest paid on intercompany loans, the debt must satisfy the arm's length interest rate and the 2:1 thin capitalization ratio; otherwise interest deductions are denied and the payment may be recharacterized as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions (sales, purchases, loans, royalties, services) triggers the mandatory preparation of a Local File and Master File under Article 11 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act. All entities, regardless of size, must file the foreign related-party transaction statement (Form 2-2) with the annual corporate tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the tax authorities enforce a substance-over-form doctrine and a General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 26-8 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act) to disregard artificial or conduit arrangements. For the Korean LLC, actual business premises, employees, inventory, administrative control, and decision-making functions must be present in Korea. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for the resin statue business include design adaptation, production, quality control, warehousing, customer service, and risk management. Absent this substance, treaty claims by non-resident shareholders can be denied and the entity may be treated as a sham, resulting in recharacterisation of income, denial of deductions, and additional penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Underreporting Digital Sales Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to include preorder deposits and online payment receipts from Stripe or PayPal as gross revenue, using personal bank accounts or offshore merchant accounts to divert company sales, or intentionally concealing overseas direct-to-consumer sales of resin statues and garage kits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine of up to 5 times the tax evaded; aggravated fraudulent evasion may result in up to 10 years' imprisonment. In addition, the National Tax Service can assess a 40% civil fraud penalty under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus interest and daily surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face piercing of the corporate veil under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act, becoming jointly and severally liable for the full corporate tax deficiency. Personal civil asset restitution includes seizure of personal bank accounts, homes, and vehicles. The NTS may also place the director on a travel ban (blacklist) preventing international travel, and criminal prosecution can lead to imprisonment of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Outbound Withholding Tax on Dividends, Royalties, and Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders or paying royalties/interest to foreign related parties without withholding the statutory 22% (or applicable treaty-substituted) tax, without filing the withholding return, or without properly documenting the beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 98-4 of the Corporate Tax Act, the Korean payer is the withholding agent. Failure to withhold or remit triggers a penalty of up to 5% of the uncollected amount plus daily interest (Article 47-4(3) of the Framework Act on National Taxes). Criminal liability under Article 13 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can lead to imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine of up to twice the unremitted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors in their capacity as withholding agents are personally civilly liable for the unremitted tax, penalties, and interest. The director's personal assets can be attached, and the director may be placed on the NTS travel-ban blacklist, preventing international business travel. Criminal prosecution can result in imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance for Treaty Shopping and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean LLC as a shell without substantive business functions, using it solely as a conduit for foreign shareholders to hold IP, receive inbound licensing revenue, and shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions through inflated intercompany royalty payments, management fees, or overpriced raw-material imports, with no real economic activities in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities may invoke the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 26-8 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act and Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes) to disregard the transactional form, recharacterize income, deny treaty benefits, and impose an additional penalty of up to 30% of the reclassified tax amount. Participation in a fraudulent sham-entity scheme is punishable under Article 4 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the entity is an alter ego of its directors or non-resident shareholders. Directors face personal civil restitution for the entire tax deficiency plus interest, disqualification from serving as directors, travel bans through blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment of up to 10 years for orchestrating the fraudulent structure.
